usage: A common noun for the lotus flower; in everyday Cantonese, it sounds natural in plant, nature, and Buddhist contexts.
Often used as a modifier in compounds like 蓮花池 or 蓮花座, so learners should notice it can appear before another noun.
In Hong Kong speech, 蓮花 is more literary or descriptive than casual, so people may also just say 荷花 in some contexts depending on region and style.
Use it when talking about the flower itself, its appearance, or symbolic meanings such as purity and elegance.
